title: Elevated-Temperature Tribo-Corrosion Response of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloy.

recollection.starting_material: Likely a cast eutectic high-entropy alloy, e.g. AlCoCrFeNi2.1 or a similar Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni composition showing a duplex FCC/B2 lamellar eutectic microstructure.
recollection.intervention: Tribo-corrosion tests performed in a high-temperature molten-salt or hot aqueous environment (perhaps 0.5 M NaCl) while sliding against an alumina or Si3N4 counterface from room temperature up to ~500 °C.
recollection.structure: During testing an adherent, nanocrystalline mixed-oxide/glaze layer (rich in Al- and Cr-oxides or spinel phases) forms on the worn surface; underneath, the original lamellar FCC + B2 eutectic survives with some plastically deformed layers.
recollection.mechanism: Elevated temperature promotes rapid selective oxidation of Al/Cr that produces a protective tribo-oxide film; this film reduces direct metal–metal contact, lowering wear. Synergistic wear-corrosion damage is governed by competition between mechanical removal of the film and its dynamic re-formation.
recollection.results: Compared with room temperature, the specific wear rate drops by roughly 30–50 % at 300–400 °C (e.g. from ~7 × 10⁻⁵ to 3–4 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹) and the friction coefficient declines from ~0.65 to 0.45. Corrosion current densities measured in situ decrease by an order of magnitude once the protective glaze layer stabilizes. At >450 °C, wear rises again due to film spallation and substrate softening.

score.note: The recollection misstates the test environment and temperature range, omits the thermal-shock cycles and load/frequency protocol, and gives incorrect numerical results. It partially captures retention of the lamellar L12/FCC+B2 structure and tribo-layer formation, but overstates an adherent nanocrystalline Al/Cr-oxide glaze. The core competition between film removal and repassivation/re-formation, including reduced wear at an intermediate temperature and increased wear after film disruption, is specifically consistent with the paper.
